In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple method for estimating the rate of change of left ventricular (LV) pressure (dP/dt) from the electrocardiogram.
the development of a simple, accurate, noninvasive method for the evaluation of myocardial contractility.
a new index of the functional state and the prognosis of the left ventricular muscle in patients with acute myocardia infarction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mean electromechanical PΔt is a useful indirect index of the left ventricular peak rate of rise in pressure.

the index ΔPΔt, derived from measurement of mean arterial diastolic pressure minus left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (P) and the perejection period (PE), is a useful index of left ventricle dP/dt.

the mean electromechanical pressure-time index is an accurate and useful index of the peak left ventricular rate of rise of pressure and that it is a useful index of the functional state and prognosis of patients with acute myocardium infarction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measurement of the mean electromechanical PΔt is a useful index of the peak dP/dt of the left ventricular pressure curve and, therefore, of the functional condition of the left ventricles.

ΔPΔt is an accurate and useful index of the maximal left ventricular rate of pressure rise (dP/dt) and that it can be used to assess the functional state of left ventricular performance in acute myocardial infraction and other cardiac disorders.

the mean electromechanical preejection pressure-time index (ΔPΔt) is an accurate, indirect index of left-ventricular peak rate of rise in pressure (dP/dt), and thus of the functional state and contractile performance of the left ventricular myocardium.

the mean electromechanical PΔt index can be used to estimate dP/dt.
